extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties in PTAB inter partes review (IPR) proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, PTAB/Director staff, appellate counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and legal criteria applied when the USPTO Director reviews a PTAB Final Written Decision in an inter partes review, especially as to the treatment and weight of expert testimony and resulting remedies (vacatur/termination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse of discretion in crediting expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board abused its discretion by improperly crediting expert testimony that has multiple material contradictions and that the Board found lacked credibility at least in certain respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision (at 32) states: "[W]e agree with Patent Owner that Mr. Hutton’s explanation as to how his Declaration supports that combination [of Szrek and Llach] is not credible . . . ." Example: Mr. Hutton gave conflicting testimony about whether Exhibit 2050 represents the modification described in his declaration (compare deposition citations). If a credibility determination shows material contradictions, reliance on that testimony can constitute an abuse of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of evidence when relying on self-contradictory expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: When the party with the burden of proof rests its case on an expert’s self-contradictory testimony, the evidence may be insufficient to satisfy the applicable standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities: Finesse Wireless LLC v. AT&T Mobility LLC, No. 2024-1039, 2025 WL 2713518, at *4 (Fed. Cir. Sept. 24, 2025) and Johns Hopkins Univ. v. Datascope Corp., 543 F.3d 1342, 1349 (Fed. Cir. 2008). The Order explains that because the Board rested its finding of a reason to combine on Mr. Hutton’s contradictory testimony, the Board’s finding of unpatentability on the Szrek-based grounds is vacated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility on one issue affects weight on other issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony of one who has been found unreliable as to one issue may properly be accorded little weight as to subsequent issues; thus credibility findings can diminish or negate reliance on the same testimony across other grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted precedent: N.L.R.B. v. Pittsburgh S.S. Co., 337 U.S. 656, 659 (1949): "[I]n the determination of litigated facts, the testimony of one who has been found unreliable as to one issue may properly be accorded little weight as to the next." The Order applies this principle to decline reliance on Hutton’s testimony for other grounds the Board did not reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason to combine references must be supported by credible, non-contradictory testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: A finding that an ordinarily skilled artisan would have had a reason to combine disclosures of separate references cannot rest on expert testimony that is materially contradictory or non-credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete application: the Board’s finding of a reason to combine Szrek and Llach was central to the unpatentability determination and was based on Mr. Hutton’s testimony; because that testimony was contradictory, the finding was vacated. Example of contradiction: inconsistent statements about how Szrek would be modified to incorporate Llach’s transaction computer (deposition vs. declaration/inconsistent depiction in Exhibit 2050).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of vacatur and termination when central evidence is unreliable
rubrics_metrics.description: If critical evidence (e.g., an expert’s testimony) is found not credible on material aspects, it may be appropriate to vacate the Board’s Final Written Decision and terminate the proceeding rather than let the decision stand or rely on that testimony for remaining grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order vacated the Board’s Final Written Decision and terminated the proceeding because Mr. Hutton’s testimony was central and found not credible as to multiple material aspects. Authorities cited for remedial posture: Sling TV, L.L.C. v. Realtime Adaptive Streaming LLC, 840 F. App’x 598 (Fed. Cir. 2021); BioDelivery Scis. Int’l, Inc. v. Aquestive Therapeutics, Inc., 935 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on Director Review and scope based on Board’s rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Review addresses alleged errors in the Board’s decision; issues not reached by the Board may not provide a basis for Director Review absent separate grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner argued the Board did not rule on the Irwin-based grounds, so there would be no basis for Director Review on those grounds. The Order notes that other petition grounds relying on the same questionable testimony were not reached by the Board (see Decision 51), and the lack of credibility of that testimony affects those unresolved grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: This Order is not a Final Written Decision under 35 U.S.C. § 318(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Director’s Order granting review and vacating a Board decision does not itself constitute a Final Written Decision under the IPR statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly states: "This decision does not constitute a final written decision under 35 U.S.C. § 318(a)." (procedural note; no additional guidance provided).
